managed_restore.why: The PA-RR-03 bootstrap used `pg_restore --data-only --disable-triggers`, which turns off the system triggers that enforce foreign keys and is reserved for superusers. No managed PostgreSQL service grants that, so the procedure would have failed on the first real database. Replaced by an explicit dependency order applied in one transaction, demonstrated here as a role that is not a superuser.

restricted_role.name: pathable_app
restricted_role.note: Approximates DigitalOcean's doadmin: owns its databases, is not a superuser. PostGIS is created by the platform's own admin, as a managed service does; migration 0001 uses CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS, which an ordinary owner may run once the extension is present.

old_procedure_fails_as_this_role.error: permission denied: "RI_ConstraintTrigger_a_21027" is a system trigger

restore.pg_dump_natural_order_also_works: Measured: an unordered --data-only restore of this archive succeeded too, because pg_dump happened to emit a dependency-safe order for this tree-shaped schema. The order is pinned anyway so that stays true rather than remaining a coincidence.
